summary.headline: Route Mobile Q2 FY27 gross margin recovered to 22.4% from 20.9% in Q1, with revenue up 5.4% YoY to INR 1,180 crores.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose 5.4% YoY and 2.4% QoQ to INR 1,180 crores, with H1 revenue up 7.4% to INR 2,331 crores. Gross margin recovered to 22.4% after Q1's 20.9% dip, driven by higher-margin new products (RCS, WhatsApp, IP messaging), which grew 36.7% YoY to INR 128 crores and now exceed 10% of revenue. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 118.4 crores (10% margin), held back by one-off Masivian security-incident costs and a performance bonus provision; management targets a return to around 12% margin. Heltar acquisition (INR 33.7 crores total consideration) completed in July 2026 and contributed roughly INR 5 crores of revenue.

financial_highlights.change: vs 22.1% in Q2 FY26 (+30 bps YoY), vs 20.9% in Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.metric: New products revenue (RCS, WhatsApp, IP messaging)
financial_highlights.change: +36.7% YoY, +35.8% QoQ; >10% of revenue vs ~8% a year ago

financial_highlights.value: 47.6 billion in Q2; 93.4 billion in H1

segments.name: New products (RCS, WhatsApp, IP messaging)
segments.commentary: INR 128 crores in Q2, up 36.7% YoY and 35.8% QoQ, now over 10% of revenue; management says these carry higher margins than core messaging.

segments.name: Enterprise messaging / BFSI
segments.commentary: BFSI is the largest vertical at 15% of revenue, followed by digital natives at 12%. Heltar added AI-native no-code engagement capabilities sold via Route and Proximus sales teams.

segments.name: Operator business / Firewall
segments.commentary: AI-driven Firewall Solutions deployed at 12 operators. Firewall is a single-digit percentage of revenue; blended gross margin 50-60%, with some customers near 70%.

segments.name: ILD / long-distance
segments.commentary: Still under growth pressure: softness from a specific aggregator on inbound ILD, partly offset by direct enterprise volume. Management said it is not a growth market at present.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of mid-to-high single digit reconfirmed at the midrange, per CFO.
Adjusted EBITDA margin targeted to recover to around 12% as one-offs (Masivian security incident, performance bonus provision) moderate; management said this implies about 6% EBITDA growth YoY.
H2 levers cited: seasonal uplift in OND, conversion of high-margin firewall and new-product pipeline, and continuous cost optimisation.
Management expects volumes to rise in the OND quarter on festive and e-commerce campaigns, but declined to give a longer-term volume forecast.
Free cash of about INR 1,150-1,200 crores; capital primarily earmarked for inorganic expansion (Latam, Southeast Asia, Western markets, KSA), with dividends marginal.
capex_capacity: Heltar acquired via slump sale: BTA signed 13 July 2026, completed 29 July 2026; INR 23.9 crores paid at closing from internal accruals, INR 9.8 crores deferred 18 months.
Firewall solutions live at 12 operators with a healthy pipeline; network API being developed with the Proximus Global ecosystem.
Masivian (Colombia) received a new CEO (Marko Erkic); Q3 expected to be seasonally strong for Masivian post-breach.
Acquisition pipeline: conversational AI targets in Latin America and Southeast Asia; management says early-stage, no agreement reached.
demand_pricing: RCS pricing increased by telcos effective 1 September 2026; management says marketing message rates have roughly doubled, while utility and authentication pricing changed marginally. WhatsApp pricing unchanged.
Management said RCS volumes remain healthy so far, but the long-run impact depends on brand ROI; the SMS/WhatsApp/RCS split for the festive season is still uncertain.
Long-distance inbound to India is flattish; outbound from India to other countries is picking up via a couple of bank contracts.
Top 5 customers were 30% of revenue vs 33% a year ago; 80 customers exceed USD 1 million annual billing vs 73 in FY26.
Heltar early wins across banking, healthcare, retail, consumer durables and education; Middle East and Latin America opportunities emerging.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of nonrecurring revenue, and how much of H1 NRR is recurring versus one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nonrecurring revenue is mainly one-time campaigns and product-development charges with seasonality, especially the OND bump; it could not give an exact split and will do a deep dive. GRR for H1 was not disclosed and will be sent offline.

qa_highlights.question: Expected volume growth in coming quarters after the plateau around 45 billion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a long-term forecast but expects slightly improved volumes in OND as festive and e-commerce communication rises.

qa_highlights.question: Cash deployment and M&A focus; RCS and WhatsApp pricing changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Free cash is about INR 1,150-1,200 crores; dividends are marginal and acquisitions are the priority, mainly in Latam and Southeast Asia, with KSA and Western markets also considered. RCS prices rose from 1 September, with marketing rates nearly doubled; WhatsApp unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 12% EBITDA margin target achievable and what is the bridge from 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO reconfirmed mid-to-high single-digit revenue guidance and said the 10% margin excludes meaningful one-offs, so it rises on a normalised basis; H2 levers include seasonality, high-margin pipeline conversion and cost optimisation.

qa_highlights.question: How much of new-product growth is organic versus acquired, and is any of it one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Heltar contributed about mid-single-digit revenue, roughly INR 5 crores, in the quarter; the rest is organic. Management says the growth is recurring, not campaign-driven.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for ILD and the Claro relationship; firewall economics?
qa_highlights.answer: ILD growth remains difficult, with softness from one aggregator partly offset by direct deals. Claro revenue existed in Q1 and has stabilised as a firewall customer. Firewall is single-digit % of revenue with 50-60% blended gross margin and some advanced conversions expected in coming quarters.

risks_watch: Adjusted EBITDA margin at 10% vs 12% target; recovery depends on one-offs fading and H2 pipeline conversion.
RCS price increase from 1 September 2026 may shift brand spend away from RCS or reduce ROI over the long run.
ILD business under pressure from aggregator softness; management is not confident of growth.
Client concentration (top 5 at 30%) and nonrecurring revenue share with limited disclosure; GRR not yet provided.
Masivian security incident aftermath and the scale of Heltar/Latam acquisitions still under evaluation.
summary.management_tone: Confident on gross margin and new products, but cautious on ILD, RCS pricing impact and volume visibility. Management was evasive on the nonrecurring revenue split and the quantum of future M&A, deferring answers offline.
key_quotes: Gross margin recovered to 22.4% in quarter 2 from 20.9% in quarter 1.
As I said then, this was not business we had lost.
These one-off costs do not impact the run rate and will moderate and return to normal levels in the coming periods.

growth.why: Revenue guidance of mid-to-high single digit (midpoint ~7%) reconfirmed for FY27, backed partly by new products (INR 128 crores, +36.7% YoY), Heltar acquisition, firewall pipeline and RCS price increases, but no specific capacity or order numbers were given; EBITDA margin recovery to ~12% in H2 FY27 is guided, with Q2 adjusted EBITDA up 8.7% QoQ and reported EBITDA YoY growth not stated.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Adjusted EBITDA margin at 10% in Q2 vs guided ~12% recovery as Masivian and bonus one-offs fade; gross margin recovered to 22.4% from 20.9% in Q1 on higher-margin new products (INR 128 crores, >10% of revenue).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management expects slightly higher volumes in OND on festive and e-commerce campaigns; H1 billable transactions up about 11% YoY to 93.4 billion, though ILD is flattish and no long-term volume forecast was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure disclosed and no capex plan; cash of INR 1,150-1,200 crores is earmarked mainly for inorganic deals (Latam, Southeast Asia, KSA, West), so announcements would be acquisitions rather than capacity capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Revenue guidance of mid-to-high single digit was only reconfirmed at midrange (about 7%) and H1 revenue growth of 7.4% sits at that level, leaving no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: RCS price increase from 1 September 2026 (marketing message rates roughly doubled), ILD softness from one aggregator, and EBITDA at 10% vs 12% target could pressure the midrange guide if one-offs persist.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Firewall network API being developed with Proximus Global, Heltar AI-native no-code engagement capabilities being sold via Route and Proximus sales teams, and RCS/WhatsApp/IP messaging grew 36.7% YoY to INR 128 crores.

rows.label: RCS price increase by telcos
rows.why: Telco RCS pricing rose effective 1 September 2026 with marketing message rates roughly doubled; WhatsApp unchanged and utility/authentication marginal, so it is a tailwind to revenue per message but could shift brand spend away from RCS.

rows.label: Heltar integration and early wins
rows.why: Heltar completed 29 July 2026 and contributed about INR 5 crores in Q2; early wins across banking, healthcare, retail, consumer durables and education, with Middle East and Latin America opportunities emerging.

rows.label: Dividends marginal, cash for M&A
rows.why: Free cash of about INR 1,150-1,200 crores is earmarked mainly for inorganic expansion; the Heltar deferred INR 9.8 crores payment falls due in 18 months, and no M&A agreement has been reached yet.

tone.note: Management was confident on gross margin recovery, new products and the 12% EBITDA target, but cautious on ILD, RCS pricing impact and volume visibility; analysts pressed on the nonrecurring revenue split and the scale of future M&A, which management deferred offline.
